state.case_summary:
A 58-year-old man presented with abdominal pain that began around the umbilicus 2 days earlier and migrated to the right lower quadrant. He had no prior abdominal surgeries or systemic disease. He denied anorexia, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, weight loss, night sweats, diarrhea, or constipation. On examination, he was afebrile; heart rate was 86 bpm, and blood pressure was 130/95 mm Hg. Abdominal examination showed voluntary guarding in the right lower quadrant and minimal tenderness elsewhere. Laboratory tests revealed a white-cell count of 15,600/mL, hemoglobin of 14.2 g/dL, and platelet count of 126,000/mL. Plain abdominal X-rays demonstrated several air–fluid levels without free air under the diaphragm. Ultrasound assessment was interpreted as compatible with plastron appendicitis. Computed tomography of the abdomen revealed a linear lesion within the intestinal lumen in the right lower quadrant, causing partial luminal obliteration and edema on the anterolateral aspect of the cecum.

What is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. Small intestinal perforation
B. such a patient
C. Acute appendicitis was considered because of the migratory periumbilical to right lower quadrant pain and leukocytosis
D. Plastron appendicitis was entertained based on ultrasound findings
E. Peptic ulcer perforation was less likely given the absence of free intraperitoneal air on X
F. Foreign
G. Other rare causes (urinary tract pathology, inflammatory bowel disease, intestinal parasitosis, malignancy, Meckel’s
H. None

root.label: Subacute Abdominal Pain Syndrome with Right Lower Quadrant Tenderness and Elevated White-Cell Count
supporting_facts: abdominal pain migrating to the right lower quadrant
voluntary guarding in the right lower quadrant
several air–fluid levels on plain abdominal X-rays
ultrasound assessment compatible with plastron appendicitis
computed tomography showing a linear lesion within the intestinal lumen in the right lower quadrant
excluded_candidates: Gastroenteritis: less likely due to the absence of diarrhea, vomiting, and systemic symptoms
Inflammatory bowel disease: less likely due to the acute onset and absence of prior abdominal symptoms
alarm_features: elevated white-cell count indicating possible infection or inflammation
salient_findings: abdominal pain migrating to the right lower quadrant

B1.label: Infectious/inflammatory cause
askable_discriminators: Does the patient have a fever?
Has the patient recently traveled or been exposed to anyone with a similar illness?

B2.label: Mechanical/obstructive cause
askable_discriminators: Has the patient experienced any nausea or vomiting?
Has the patient had any abdominal surgeries in the past?

B3.label: Vascular cause
askable_discriminators: Has the patient experienced any recent trauma or injury?
Has the patient had any history of vascular disease?

B4.label: Other rare causes
askable_discriminators: Has the patient experienced any recent travel or exposure to unusual pathogens?
Has the patient had any history of rare or exotic diseases?
